facts.fact: Chami (a drover) and Rajan (a boy from Kalladi with a spear taller than himself) are the two other volunteers killed on the shelf, with Sankaran, on the first day.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires three volunteer dead and only Sankaran is named.

facts.fact: Thurai ladders are lashed ship-timber with iron hooks, and the Thurai wear bronze caps; the assault is about three hundred men.
facts.why: needed to describe the dawn assault.

facts.fact: Kandan's men keep the names of the dead on a chalked roof tile, in imitation of Neela's barracks name tile.
facts.why: needed because Devan must receive the dead names at the evening count.

facts.fact: Muthu writes his thirty-man sortie in the open post book in black wax and plain ink as 'to escort refugees from the pass villages', and takes the thirty from the garrison without the fort's full strength being counted.
facts.why: needed to explain how Muthu's written order lets him come down under the crown's order that the garrison stay inside the walls.

facts.fact: Kesu's village is at the foot of the goat path, a half day below the shelf and behind the Thurai lines; the herald names it as the first to burn at dawn.
facts.why: needed to set up the herald's threat and the chapter's out-question.

facts.fact: On the first noon Devan felt a sting on his left thumb mid-fight but could not count it; on the second noon he sees three clear welts and sits on a boulder until they fade.
facts.why: needed to reconcile the beat's 'at noon the next day' with the standing noon signal from ch 10.
